html:
The Ocaina are a small Indigenous people of the Amazon forest on the border of Peru and Colombia, originally along the Igaraparaná and Putumayo rivers. They speak a Witotoan language, related to that of their Huitoto neighbours.

In the early 1900s the Ocaina were among the peoples enslaved and killed by the Peruvian Amazon Company to collect wild rubber, the Putumayo atrocities exposed by Roger Casement. Survivors were moved, and many now live on the Ampiyacu river in Peru. Their neighbours include the Miraña.
